name: Sorrel Basin Groundwater Allocation Plan

source_sentences: The plan caps the groundwater pumped from the basin at 210,000 af a year (70% of the 2017 to 2021 average), binding holders of non-domestic wells.
Domestic wells pumping under 2 af a year are exempt.
Shares may be sold, and a year's allocation leased, separately from land.
Crops are sold in national markets: the basin grows about 5% of the nation's tree nuts and under 1% of each field crop.
Meters with telemetry are required on every non-domestic well by 1 October 2027, at the owner's cost (about $3,000 a well); readings are monthly; satellite checks of crop water use are made.
The penalty is $600 per af pumped over allocation, with loss of shares for repeated violation.
The SBWA is funded by an annual fee of $10 per af of shares held (about $2.1 million a year).
No expiry; the cap is reviewed in 2032.
The Sorrel Basin Water Authority (SBWA) published its draft plan, including the 2017 to 2021 base period, on 15 March 2022.
About 6,000 people work on farms in the basin.

90% of the cap (189,000 af) is issued by the SBWA as permanent shares of the annual cap, to whoever holds a parcel on 1 July 2027, in proportion to the parcel's average metered or estimated pumping in water years 2017 to 2021.
A holder receives about 63% of its history.
Before March 2022 no allocation method had been proposed in the basin; the state's groundwater act allows allocation by history, by area or by auction.
10% of the cap (21,000 af) is issued by the SBWA as permanent shares in blocks of 100 af, drawn by lottery in September 2027.
Eligible: each parcel of at least 20 acres in the basin, held on 1 July 2027, with no K2 allocation; one entry per parcel; entry fee $500.

unclear.text: Trading across sub-basins: whether a share may be pumped only in the sub-basin where its parcel lies, or anywhere in the basin.
readings: U1-a: a share may be pumped only from a well in the sub-basin where the parcel that earned it lies
U1-b: a share may be pumped anywhere in the basin; the impact rules only set conditions on individual wells (spacing, monitoring)

context: Average pumping in water years 2017 to 2021 was about 300,000 acre-feet (af) a year: North 110,000 (mostly field crops: cotton, alfalfa, grain), Central 70,000 (mixed), South 120,000 (mostly tree nuts).
The survey estimates the basin's long-run sustainable yield at about 200,000 af a year.
Over 2017 to 2021 the water table fell about 2.5 feet a year on average and about 4 feet a year in South.

About 2,400 agricultural wells and about 4,000 domestic wells draw on the aquifer; about 60 agricultural wells a year were deepened or replaced (about $80,000 each), and about 150 domestic wells went dry in 2017 to 2021.
The county runs an emergency water program for households with dry wells.
The Sorrel Irrigation District delivers canal water to about 30,000 acres in North; surface water also trades between districts in the region, at about $250 per af in normal years.
To the east, the Lowther Basin has no cap; its plan is due in 2030.
